content:
Worked request/response examples for the common Subscriber API flows. All paths are relative to `https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier`; every request carries `X-API-Key: <your-key>`.


## Create a subscriber

`subscriberNumber` is the only **required** field (your operator's own reference, 1-32 characters); `name` is optional. A subscriber is created as identity only, with no gateway host. Each call creates a new subscriber.

```
curl -X POST "https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier/subscribers" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "subscriberNumber": "SUB-10012",
    "name": "Acme Store #12",
    "email": "ops@acme.example",
    "serviceAddress": "12 Main St, Springfield, 01101, US",
    "metadata": {"tier": "gold"}
  }'
```

```
{
  "data": {
    "id": "3f9a1c2e-8b4d-4f21-9a7c-1d2e3f4a5b6c",
    "orgId": "0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d",
    "subscriberNumber": "SUB-10012",
    "name": "Acme Store #12",
    "email": "ops@acme.example",
    "notes": null,
    "serviceAddress": "12 Main St, Springfield, 01101, US",
    "planId": null,
    "hostId": null,
    "state": "pending_assignment",
    "suspended": false,
    "metadata": {"tier": "gold"},
    "createdAt": "2026-07-16T18:00:00Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-07-16T18:00:00Z"
  },
  "traceId": "8b23d81344dbdcd29f92ddf26c4a2a07"
}
```

The minimum body is just the subscriber number:

```
curl -X POST "https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier/subscribers" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"subscriberNumber": "SUB-10013"}'
```


## List subscribers

Cursor-paginated. Pass `pageSize` (alias of `limit`, max 500) and follow `meta.nextCursor` until it is absent. You can also filter (`planId`, `suspended`) and sort (`sort=name` or `sort=-createdAt`; omitted = newest first).

```
curl "https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier/subscribers?pageSize=50&sort=name" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

```
{
  "data": [
    { "id": "3f9a1c2e-…", "subscriberNumber": "SUB-10012", "name": "Acme Store #12", "state": "installed", "hostId": "70A7…" }
  ],
  "meta": { "nextCursor": "eyJ…", "limit": 50, "hasMore": true },
  "traceId": "8b23…"
}
```

Next page (the cursor is valid only for the same `sort`):

```
curl "https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier/subscribers?pageSize=50&sort=name&cursor=eyJ…" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```


## Get one subscriber

Returns the full subscriber.

```
curl "https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier/subscribers/3f9a1c2e-…" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```


## Update a subscriber

`PATCH` with only the fields you want to change. Each field is three-state:

| Field | Absent | JSON `null` | A value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | unchanged | **clears it** | must be non-empty after trimming, ≤128 bytes |
| `email` | unchanged | **clears it** | must be a valid address, ≤255 bytes |
| `notes` | unchanged | **clears it** | ≤4096 bytes |
| `serviceAddress` | unchanged | **clears it** | replaced verbatim, ≤1024 bytes |
| `planId` | unchanged | **clears the plan** | must be an assignable plan in your organization |
| `subscriberNumber` | unchanged | `400 validation_failed` | 1–32 characters after trimming |
| `metadata` | unchanged | unchanged (**not** a clear) | replaces the whole document, ≤8 KiB |

Two things worth calling out. `subscriberNumber` is the one field that cannot be cleared — `null`, `""` and whitespace are all a `400` naming the field, so a clear is never silently swallowed. And `metadata` is a whole-document replace rather than a merge: `null` leaves it alone, and `\{\}` is how you empty it.

Length limits on the free-text fields are counted in **bytes of UTF-8**, not characters, so a name in a multi-byte script reaches the 128 limit sooner than 128 visible characters.

```
curl -X PATCH "https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier/subscribers/3f9a1c2e-…" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Acme Store #12 (Downtown)", "notes": null}'
```


## Attach / detach the gateway host

The response carries the updated subscriber under `data` plus a sibling `prevHostId` — the host that was linked immediately before the call (null for a fresh attach; the replaced host on a re-link; the removed host on detach).

**Neither verb is idempotent.** A call whose requested end state already holds is rejected with `409`, and nothing is written — the API does not answer `200` for work it did not do:

| Call | Result | `prevHostId` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PUT` on a subscriber with no host | `200` attached | `null` |
| `PUT` with the host already attached to this subscriber | `409 gateway_already_attached` | — |
| `PUT` with a host held by a *different* subscriber | `409 gateway_already_linked` | — |
| `PUT` with a different, unheld host | `200` re-linked in place (RMA) | the replaced host |
| `DELETE` with a host linked | `200` detached | the removed host |
| `DELETE` with no host linked | `409 no_attached_host` | — |

Because a repeat is an error rather than a no-op, do not blindly retry one of these calls after a network timeout. Either re-read the subscriber first (`GET /subscribers/\{id\}`, field `hostId`) and act on what you find, or treat `409 gateway_already_attached` / `409 no_attached_host` as "already applied" — both mean the link is in the state you were trying to reach.

```
# attach (or re-link) a gateway host to the subscriber
curl -X PUT "https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier/subscribers/3f9a1c2e-…/host" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"hostId": "70A7..."}'


# detach
curl -X DELETE "https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier/subscribers/3f9a1c2e-…/host" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

```
{
  "data": { "id": "3f9a1c2e-…", "hostId": "70A7...", "state": "installed" },
  "prevHostId": null,
  "traceId": "…"
}
```

```
{
  "error": {
    "code": "no_attached_host",
    "message": "subscriber has no attached gateway host to detach"
  },
  "traceId": "…"
}
```


## Assign a service plan

```
curl -X PUT "https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier/subscribers/3f9a1c2e-…/plan" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"planId": "a62b7c4d-…"}'
```

Assigning an archived plan returns `400 service_plan_archived`; an unknown plan returns `404 service_plan_not_found`.


## Suspend / resume service

Both are idempotent — repeating them returns `200` with the current state. The suspend body (`reason`) is optional.

```
curl -X POST "https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier/subscribers/3f9a1c2e-…/suspend" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"reason": "non-payment"}'


curl -X POST "https://api.ui.com/v1/carrier/subscribers/3f9a1c2e-…/resume" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

See [Error Handling](https://developer.ui.com/carrier-fabric/v1.0.0/error-handling) for failure responses.
